analysis.title: Following AI's $1.6 trillion Money Trail: Mapping the Revenue Generated by the Capex Boom
key_insights: MS maps $1.6T of 2027 hyperscaler and neocloud AI capex (cash plus lease) to $1.7T of supplier revenues across about 50 companies. Total capex is $980B in 2026 (+~100% y/y), $1.6T in 2027 (+~60%) and $1.8T in 2028 (+14%).

New lease capex estimates add $195B to 2027 and $246B to 2028. Cash capex of $1.4T in 2027 rises 14% to $1.58T of total capex. Hyperscalers disclose more than $1.1T of leases signed but not yet started.

MS tracks about 65% of AI capex flowing into S&P 500 revenue ($1.0T of $1.58T in 2027). That is 5% of 2027 SPX sales and about 24-25% of 2027 SPX sales growth. SPX sales growth is 8.6% with AI capex and 6.6% without it.
NVDA takes about two-thirds of the AI capex revenue absorbed by the S&P 500 (about $690B of $1.0T in 2027). Ex-NVDA flow-through is $339B, or 1.6% of 2027 SPX sales.

The 42 'Core to Thesis' AI names in the SPX grow 2027 sales 28% vs 5% for non-AI, and 2027 earnings 25% vs 4%. They drive 60% of 2027 SPX sales growth and 78% of 2027 earnings growth, and make up 37% of 2027 consensus net income. The Magnificent 7 are about 75% of AI-cohort earnings.
Both AI and non-AI cohorts peaked in earnings growth in 2Q26. MS says markets trade on rate of change and expects leadership to shift from pure Enablers toward blended Enabler/Adopters and Adopters.

Hyperscaler capex is expected to add about 70 GW of compute capacity in 2027-28 (32 GW in 2027, 38 GW in 2028), reaching about 123-145 GW by 2028, roughly 4x 2025. Custom ASICs rise from 34% of incremental capacity in 2025 to 66% in 2028, led by Trainium and TPU (12 GW combined vs 13 GW for NVDA in 2028).

MS puts incremental ROIC on AI spend at 25-50%: about 25-40% for GPU rental (IaaS, 60-70% incremental EBIT margin) and 40%+ for a model-enabled API on owned infrastructure (70%+ margin). MS is bullish AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT and META.

Hyperscalers generate about $1T of combined operating cash flow in each of 2027 and 2028. In a slowdown, the bull case is positive FCF revisions and a multiple re-rate. The bear case is overcapacity, D&A deleverage and a de-rating.

Semis: MS expects hyperscaler investment to keep favoring large caps, led by NVDA as revenue per GW scales beyond $40-50B, with AVGO and memory also strong. NVDA is the best risk/reward as the market questions 2027 AI capex, at 15x FY28 EPS. A $1T XPU market is expected by 2028.

MS argues consensus NVDA-related estimates for SPCX and AWS are conservative. NVDA's hyperscaler segment implies other hyperscaler spend growing only 21% in 2027, vs consensus capex growth of 39% for MSFT, ORCL, META and GOOG.

Memory: the cycle enters its late stage in 4Q26 but is not ending. Price increases moderate, inventories rise and supply grows, which limits further earnings surprises. International memory stocks trade at about 3x NTM P/E. Part of recent capex raises is memory price, not volume (Amazon's CFO attributed most of its capex lift from $200B to about $220B to memory costs).

Long-term agreements change the shape of a memory downturn, which would look like a volume air pocket at a held price. In the 2022 downturn, shipments fell about 5% while prices fell 20-30%. SK hynix is buying back and cancelling W40tn of shares. Samsung set a W90-110tn 2026 shareholder return.

Networking captures about $0.25 of each incremental capex dollar, with about $0.15 coming from hyperscalers and neoclouds. Hyperscaler-linked networking revenue across 15 companies rises from $62.6B in CY25 to $237B in CY27E. Networking's share of capex falls from about 36% to about 27%. Each 10-point change in hyperscaler share moves CY27E revenue by about $38B.

Optical risks: InP laser and transceiver capacity could create oversupply, diminishing performance gains from faster links could lengthen upgrade cycles, and 1.6T/3.2T transceivers, silicon photonics, CPO and copper could cut optical content per unit of bandwidth.

EDA: Synopsys' royalty-based application-optimised IP raises its sensitivity to hyperscaler custom silicon volumes. Cadence and Synopsys have underperformed the S&P 500 YTD on 'AI disrupted' fears that MS calls overdone. A deep semis downturn is a risk, as are export controls and Chinese competition.

Hardware: DELL (Equal-weight) is the largest hyperscaler/neocloud profit exposure, with about $6.6B of CY27 gross profit on about $123B of revenue (AI servers about $119B of revenue and $5.5B of gross profit). HPE (OW) has about $2.1B of gross profit on $6.3B of revenue. SNX (OW) has about $1.5B of gross profit (about 24% of total) from Hyve. STX and WDC (both OW) have about $30B of combined hyperscale revenue in CY27.

Taiwan ODMs: value-add per rack rises 35-40% on VR200 vs GB300 while rack ASP almost doubles. ODMs earn only 4-6% margin on component cost. Hon Hai's August 2026 sales rose 52% y/y to NT$921.8B, and cloud and networking exceeded half of 2Q26 sales. ODMs trade below their 20-year average 2027E P/E of 11.5x. Consignment lowers reported revenue but raises margins, and funding needs prompted Quanta and Wistron to raise equity.
Consensus Big Four CSP capex growth is about 90% y/y this year, ~42% in 2027 and ~11% in 2028. The key investor debate for hardware is 2028 visibility and funding.

Multi-industry: VRT is the most data-center exposed (about 90% of F'27 revenue) and ETN about 33%, FPS about 65%, HUBB about 8%, TT about 20%, JCI about 20%, CARR about 12%. Backlogs cover most of 2027. The debate is 2030 durability. Risks are execution, hyperscaler insourcing, lead-time normalization for FPS, and chiller content.

Machinery: EROC is the most levered to hyperscaler spending, followed by CMI and CAT. Large-displacement engines are sold out through at least 1H28. Second-order beneficiaries include TEX, OSK, URI, DE, CNH, WSC, aggregates (VMC, MLM, CRH) and Target Hospitality.

Power: GEV gas turbines are sold out through 2029, with pricing up to $3,000/kW from $1,000/kW. Data center is a third of its pipeline. OEMs require 20-40% deposits and take orders out to 2032. Industry capacity is heading to about 150 GW a year vs ~50 GW in 2024, which raises oversupply risk. MS expects a flight to Tier 1 suppliers GEV, INIO and BE.

Financing: the cash-flow deficit peaks in 2027. Hyperscalers issued about $255B of unsecured bonds YTD in 2026, around 30% of estimated full-year capex. All-in yields are 100-180bp higher since year-end 2025, with Treasury moves about 70-80% of the widening for AMZN and GOOGL.

High-quality hyperscalers (AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT) have interest coverage above 30x (11.9x pro forma after $400B of issuance at 7%). Lower-quality ones (ORCL, SPCX) fall from 4.0x to 1.8x pro forma. Neoclouds are the most sensitive to debt costs. The 2027 issuance mix should skew to shorter-duration and asset-backed debt, with supply still concentrated in the US IG market.
Upside risks: Wall Street has underestimated secular compute cycles by an average of 38%. Bottlenecks and faster AI adoption could also lift spending.

Downside risks: policy pushback on data centers is a midterm election wedge issue, and MS's base case is a conditional buildout with no federal pause. MS sees sentiment best under a Republican sweep and worst under a Democratic sweep. Tax breaks are the consensus target.
A simultaneous fall in volume and price is underappreciated. Even a plateau in capex could hit pricing power and upstream margins quickly while volumes hold up, as in the 2022 memory downturn.

Power is the most tangible bottleneck. The $1.6T estimate assumes every chip gets powered, but MS Powering AI sees a 32 GW net US shortfall through 2028 (34% of the 97 GW needed) and about 72 GW through 2029. Memory, networking, optical and ODM builds are most exposed to a pause, while power-solution providers are relative beneficiaries.

sector_views.rationale: Hyperscaler investment continues to accrue to large-cap semis led by NVDA, with strength in AVGO and memory. Multiple compression since July means upward capex revisions could address cycle-longevity concerns.
Cycle moves into its late stage in 4Q26 but is not ending. Price increases moderate and supply rises, which limits upside earnings surprises. Stocks trade at about 3x NTM P/E.
Backlogs cover the bulk of 2027 and supply is constrained. Key debates are 2030 durability, commoditization and hyperscaler insourcing.
Turbines sold out through 2029, orders placed to 2032, deposits of 20-40%. Tier 1 suppliers (GEV, INIO, BE) are the most de-risked.
Power generation is the most direct flow-through (EROC, CMI, CAT). Second-order beneficiaries include construction equipment, aggregates and workforce lodging.
HDD vendors and AI server OEMs are the main conduits for hyperscaler capex. The debate is 2028 visibility and funding.
Value-add per rack rises 35-40% on VR200 but the market worries about 2028 and margin dilution. Trade below the 20-year average 2027E P/E of 11.5x.
AI-disruption fears are overdone and custom silicon broadens the opportunity for Synopsys and Cadence.
Networking captures a steady $0.25 per incremental capex dollar. Street assumes hyperscaler share keeps rising to 59%. Estimate risk is concentrated in the most hyperscaler-exposed names.

earnings_insights: No company earnings were reported in this note. All company-level figures are MS forecasts for CY27 or F'27, not reported results.
MS estimate: AI names in the SPX grow 2027 net income 25% vs 4% for SPX ex-AI. S&P 500 net income grows 12% in 2027 after 36% in 2026 (consensus-based, FactSet).
MS estimate: SPX sales growth of 12.2% in 2026 and 8.6% in 2027. Growth excluding AI capex is 11.0% in 2026 and 6.6% in 2027.

MS estimate: DELL CY27 gross profit of about $6.6B from T2 CSPs and neoclouds on about $123B revenue. HPE about $2.1B gross profit on about $6.3B revenue. SNX about $1.5B gross profit on about $19.8B revenue.

MS estimate: Hon Hai guided AI rack shipments up a high double-digit percent q/q in 3Q and to more than double for the year. Quanta guided 2026 AI server revenue to double. Hon Hai August 2026 sales (reported) rose 52% y/y to NT$921.8B.

Management guidance cited: VRT revenue CAGR of 20-22% through 2030. FPS total revenue growth of 76% in F'27. Nvidia guides 70% total revenue growth in FY28. SpaceX management expects to deploy 3-8 GW in 2027.

risk_factors: Power bottleneck: a 32 GW net US shortfall through 2028 could force order push-outs and stranded inventory.
Volume and price can fall together if capacity catches up or demand normalizes, as in the 2022 memory downturn (shipments about -5%, prices -20-30%).
Memory, optics, networking, ODM builds and small-dollar content (power management, analog) are most exposed to over-ordering and a pause.
Financing constraints for lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds, with ORCL and SPCX coverage falling to 1.8x pro forma.
Data center policy pushback, with tax breaks the consensus target and the midterms a catalyst.
2028 capex growth slowing to about 14% and the 2030 durability debate for power and electrical suppliers.
Hyperscaler insourcing of power and cooling products, plus execution risk on capacity expansion (ETN and VRT have already faced challenges).
Oversupply and lower optical content per unit of bandwidth from higher-speed transceivers, silicon photonics and CPO.
Headline capex growth is partly a memory-price variable, so slower contract price growth could cut capex growth with no change in build plans.

tension_points.bull_case: Attractive 25-50% incremental ROIC, a capex forecast history that Wall Street has underestimated by an average of 38%, and about $1T of annual operating cash flow support continued investment. The index still grows 6.6% without AI capex.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth drops from about 100% to about 60% to about 14% by 2028, free cash flow turns most negative in 2027, financing strains lower-rated borrowers, and returns could disappoint with overcapacity risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI returns disappointing, with utilization and monetization falling short of expectations and capex slowing. A plateau in capex would hit memory and component pricing before volumes.

tension_points.bull_case: DRAM is a key AI bottleneck, long-term agreements cover at least 90% of hyperscaler DRAM demand, and stocks trade at about 3x NTM P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: The cycle is late stage with price increases moderating from 4Q26, rising inventories and supply growth (including CXMT), and a downturn could look like a volume air pocket at a held price.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A plateau in hyperscaler capex or y/y contract price growth rolling over, which memory stocks have historically anticipated by about four months.

tension_points.bull_case: Backlogs cover the bulk of 2027, orders extend to 2032 with 20-40% deposits, and pipeline commentary indicates durability through 2030.
tension_points.bear_case: Capacity expansions heading to about 150 GW a year raise oversupply risk, project conversion faces power, labor and supply chain limits, and newer entrants face cancellation risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A demand downturn driven by reduced hyperscaler and utility capex, which would soften pricing and cut utilization.

tension_points.bull_case: Value-add per rack rises 35-40% on VR200 vs GB300, and GPUs and ASICs will coexist.
tension_points.bear_case: Value-add grows more slowly than rack ASP, working capital needs force equity raises, and 2028 capex growth falls to about 11% in consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Consignment spreading slowly, which would decide whether 2027 revenue estimates hold.
